lessons.title: Vibrato
body: The LFO is a slow, invisible finger wobbling a knob for you, several times per second. Right now it is aimed at the pitch.
Depth decides how wide the wobble is. A little vibrato sounds human, like a violinist. Too much sounds like a siren.

goal.hint: Give the note a singer's vibrato - gentle and human, not a siren.

lessons.title: The slow sweep
body: The same invisible finger can ride the cutoff knob instead of the pitch. Then the brightness pulses while the note stays still.
Rate decides how fast it rides. Find the slow, breathing sweep - a wave rolling in, not a machine gun.

goal.hint: Slow it down until the brightness breathes - a rolling wave, not a flutter.
